review.summary: AI mandate intact with steady holds amid chip pullback; MU profit strong while others stable.
what_worked: MU thesis validated with 26% gain and continued hold on HBM demand
Consistent hold decisions across NVDA/AMD/TSM without over-trading
AVGO closed to reallocate within AI (to broader exposure)
mistakes_or_risks: Portfolio concentrated in 4 semi-related names (memory/GPU/foundry) with similar entry timing
No explicit stop-loss triggers executed despite VIX and pullback signals
Missed potential intra-AI rotation (e.g., equipment or ETF) during 6/9 dip
next_improvements: Define and apply take-profit/stop-loss rules for winners like MU
Monitor for re-entry or new AI mandate names (e.g., equipment/ASIC) on further weakness
Track position sizing to cap single-ticker exposure below 30%
risk_notes: MU unrealized gain >25% warrants profit-taking discipline
All positions opened late-May; correlated beta to chip cycle
Cash buffer available but no new deployments in today's session
